## 2. Analysis (agent, schema-validated)
Legacy R script fits GLM1 of the Noll/Salzmann/Wuthrich (2018) freMTPL2 case study: a Poisson claim-frequency GLM (log link) with offset log(Exposure) on a 90% learn sample. Features: VehPowerGLM (factor, VehPower capped at 9), VehAgeGLM (3 classes, ref '2'), DrivAgeGLM (7 age bands, ref '5'), BonusMalusGLM (capped at 150, continuous), VehBrand (factor, ref B1), VehGas (factor), DensityGLM (log Density), Region (factor, ref R24), AreaGLM (Area A..F as integer 1..6). 49 coefficients, converged in 6 IRLS iterations.

**Randomness:** set.seed(100); ll <- sample(1:nrow(dat), round(0.9*nrow(dat))) gives a 90/10 learn/test split. Not re-implemented: the frozen split from the R capture (model/reference/split.csv) is supplied by the harness (R-RNG-01).

| # | R code | What it does | Columns | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dat <- read.csv("data/freMTPL2freq.csv", quote = "\"'", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)` | Read CSV; both double and single quotes are quote characters, so surrounding single quotes on Area, VehBrand, VehGas, Region are removed. check.names=TRUE (column names already syntactic). Strings stay character. | IDpol, ClaimNb, Exposure, Area, VehPower, VehAge, DrivAge, BonusMalus, VehBrand, VehGas, Density, Region | R-IO-01, R-IO-04, R-IO-03 |

| 6 | `VehAgeGLM <- cbind(c(0:110), c(1, rep(2, 10), rep(3, 100))) dat$VehAgeGLM <- as.factor(Veh` | Lookup table: VehAge 0 -> 1, 1..10 -> 2, 11..110 -> 3; factor then relevel reference to '2' (levels 2,1,3). Positional column 2 of the lookup matrix is the class code; dat[, "VehAgeGLM"] is a named reference. | VehAge, VehAgeGLM | R-IDX-01, R-FAC-01, R-REC-02 |

Protected attribute (age). | DrivAge, DrivAgeGLM | R-IDX-01, R-FAC-01, R-REC-02, GOV-01 |

**Protected attributes used by the legacy model (migrated faithfully per GOV-01):** DrivAge

**Risks flagged for validation:**
- GOV-01: DrivAge (age, protected characteristic) enters the model via DrivAgeGLM bands; migrated faithfully, needs actuarial justification (Equality Act 2010 Sch.3 para 20A) and fairness review.
- AreaGLM uses the integer code of a factor (as.integer(factor(Area))): depends on level sorting; treats an ordinal as linear.
- Hard-coded lookup tables: VehAge > 110 or DrivAge outside 18..100 would make R fail (subscript out of bounds) or produce wrong rows; Python maps such values to NaN (no prediction). No such values affected the R run.
- Data error treatments (ClaimNb capped at 4, Exposure capped at 1) are judgemental and applied before the split.
- Region / VehBrand levels absent in future data, or new levels, cannot be scored (NaN in Python; R predict would error).
- Reproducibility of the split depends on R's RNG (sample.kind Rejection, R >= 3.6); split frozen from capture.
- Source is a reconstruction of the published case study, not the original notebook.

## 3. Plan and rule coverage (G-13)
| # | R construct | Python approach | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | read.csv(quote = "\"'", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), check.names=TRUE | pd.read_csv(csv_path) keeping RangeIndex; apply make.names to column names; for every string column (pd.api.types.is_string_dtype) strip one pair of surrounding single quotes as R does. Never sort/reset_index. | R-IO-01, R-IO-04, R-IO-03 |
| 2 | pmin caps on ClaimNb (4) and Exposure (1) | Series.clip(upper=...) in the R order, before any feature derivation. | R-REC-02 |
| 3 | as.integer(factor(Area)); as.factor(pmin(VehPower, 9)); lookup-table recodes for VehAge and DrivAge; relevel(); pmin(BonusMalus,150); log(Density); relevel(as.factor(VehBrand/Region)); as.factor(VehGas) | AreaGLM = 1-based position of Area in its sorted unique levels; VehPowerGLM, VehAgeGLM, DrivAgeGLM kept as level strings built with explicit numpy lookup arrays (positional column 2 of the lookup matrix = class code); out-of-table values become NaN. BonusMalusGLM = clip(150); DensityGLM = np.log(Density). Factor reference levels come from meta.json xlevels (first level = reference). | R-FAC-01, R-REC-02, R-IDX-01, GOV-01 |
| 4 | model.matrix with contr.treatment and intercept | design_matrix(df): '(Intercept)' column of 1.0 first, then for each formula term in order either the numeric column or explicit 0/1 dummies '<var><level>' for every non-reference level in captured xlevels; unknown levels / NA -> NaN row. Columns == TERMS. | R-FAC-02, R-FAC-04 |
| 5 | set.seed(100); sample(); learn/test split | Not re-implemented. fit() uses only the rows it is given (frozen R split from the harness). | R-RNG-01 |
| 6 | glm(..., family = poisson(), offset = log(Exposure)), na.action = na.omit | Numpy IRLS mirroring glm.fit: mustart = y + 0.1, eta = log(mustart), z = eta - offset + (y-mu)/mu, w = sqrt(mu), QR least squares, linkinv pmax(exp(eta), DBL_EPSILON), stopping rule \|dev-devold\|/(\|dev\|+0.1) < 1e-8, maxit 25; SEs from the R factor of the last iteration's weighted QR (dispersion 1). Rows incomplete in any formula variable, response or Exposure are dropped before fitting. | R-EST-02, R-EST-03, R-NA-01 |
| 7 | predict(d.glm1, newdata = test, type = "response") | exp(X @ beta + log(Exposure)) with X from the same design_matrix; NaN wherever any input is missing, never imputed. | R-PRED-01, R-NA-01, R-EST-03 |
| 8 | DrivAge (protected) used in DrivAgeGLM | Migrated faithfully without change; recorded as a risk for validation. | GOV-01 |

## 6. Guardrails applied
- **G-01/G-02/G-03/G-04 (static, every candidate):** allowed imports only; no sklearn penalised estimators, RNG, re-splitting, `get_dummies`, shell, network, eval or file writes; interface contract; valid syntax.
- **G-05:** Python coefficient names match R's model.matrix names exactly.
- **G-06:** each candidate runs in an isolated interpreter (`python -I`) with credentials stripped from the environment and a 600s timeout.
- **G-07:** row identity holds: raw-row positions kept in order, and every row R used is present.
- **G-08:** at most 3 iterations, after which the run escalates to a human.
- **G-09:** a human must approve before release.
- **G-10:** every agent work file (analysis, plan) is validated against its schema.
- **G-11:** the agent saw the schema and level sets only, never data rows.
- **G-12:** model.yaml, thresholds.yaml, rulebook, legacy script and data were hashed at intake and re-verified before packaging.
- **G-13:** the plan cites every triggered MUST rule.
